turns.t: Hi, doctor. I'm Jordan, Casey's partner. Casey gets this pain every month, and I've been telling them to come in. ~
It's nothing, Jordan. ~
Let's hear it from you, Casey. Where's the pain? ~
Low down. On the left side, sometimes the right. Sharp. It comes and goes.
When in your cycle does it happen?
Um, about halfway. Like two weeks after my period starts.
It's the same every month. I can predict it. ~
How long does it last? ~
A day. Maybe two. ~
Is it a sharp stab, or a dull ache? ~
Sharp at first, then dull. ~
Does it get in the way of what you do? ~
It makes me curl up on the sofa. But then it's gone. ~
Any heavy bleeding with it?
No, my periods are normal.
Any fever?
No fever.
Do you have a history of cysts or gynaecological problems?
I had an ovarian cyst, a small one, a few years ago. It went away by itself.
She also gets a bit of spotting in the middle sometimes. ~
Is that right? ~
Sometimes, a tiny bit, brown. ~
Let me explain what I think is going on. Around the middle of the cycle, an egg is released from the ovary, and that can cause a sharp twinge on one side. ~
Ovulation? ~
Yes. Some women feel it every month, and it's harmless. Given the timing and the pattern, I think this is ovulation pain.
That's it? ~
That's what it sounds like. ~
Well, that's a relief. ~
Use a heat pack or a hot water bottle on your tummy, and a warm bath helps.
I'll make her a hot water bottle. ~
You'd better. ~
Pay attention to how it changes. If the pain becomes much stronger, or comes with a fever or a very heavy bleed, come back to us.
Okay. ~
Anything else you'd like to ask? ~
No. Thanks. ~
Thanks, doctor. ~
